title: Upper bounds from the heart by left completeness
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal B)$ and cohomology $H^j$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume countable products [def-weil-category-product] exist in both abelian categories and are exact, meaning that the product of every countable family of short exact sequences is short exact. Assume $D(\mathcal A)$ is left complete: for every $K$, the canonical maps $K\to\tau_{\ge -n}K$ make $K$ a derived limit of the truncation tower. Here $\tau$ denotes standard good truncation [def-kun-truncations], and a derived limit means a Roos triangle $L\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod K_n\to L[1]$, where the components of $s$ are the transition maps [def-weil-derived-limit]. Let $T:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be an exact triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category] preserving countable products with their projection maps. Let $\mathcal S$ be any class of objects of $\mathcal A$, viewed in degree zero, and let $c\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy
$$H^j(T(M[0]))=0\qquad(M\in\mathcal S,\ j>c).$$
Then for every integer $b$ and every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ such that $H^i(K)\in\mathcal S$ for every $i$ and $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$, one has
$$H^j(TK)=0\qquad(j>b+c).$$
No bound on the negative cohomological degrees of $K$, no lower amplitude bound for $T$, and no cohomological-dimension assumption on all objects of $\mathcal A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08TB, section-derived-limit, and Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; left-completeness/truncation argument extracted from blueprint det-prop-int-compactness-direct-sums proof (2). The class-relative upper-bound formulation is an agent lemma, not a quoted Stacks theorem. Product/cohomology compatibility is Tag 07KC (lemma-products); the truncation-tower discussion is Tag 0H72 (remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations).

proof.text: Put $K_n=\tau_{\ge -n}K$ for $n\ge0$, with canonical transitions $u_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$. For each integer $i$, exactness supplies $T(H^i(K)[-i])\simeq T(H^i(K)[0])[-i]$. The shift/cohomology isomorphism gives $H^j(T(H^i(K)[-i]))\simeq H^{j-i}(T(H^i(K)[0]))=0$ for $j>i+c$, by the assumed bound and $H^i(K)\in\mathcal S$. This uses the heart hypothesis only on the actual cohomology objects of $K$.

source.place: Section 05RR (section-derived-categories), cohomological shifts; Tag 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories); Homology Tags 011G (definition-shift-cochain) and 011H (definition-cohomology-shift)

proof.text:
For every integer $a\le b+1$, prove $H^j(T(\tau_{\ge a}K))=0$ for $j>b+c$ by finite induction on $b+1-a$. At $a=b+1$, all cohomology of $\tau_{\ge b+1}K$ vanishes, so the zero map from the zero complex is a quasi-isomorphism and this truncation is zero in the derived category; the additive functor $T$ sends it to zero. For the induction step use the cited lower-truncation triangle with its integer parameter equal to $-a$:
$$H^a(K)[-a]\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge a}K\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge a+1}K\longrightarrow H^a(K)[-a+1].$$
Apply $T$ and its long exact cohomology sequence. For $j>b+c$, the left term has zero $H^j$ by step 1 since $a\le b$, and the right term has zero $H^j$ by induction; hence the middle term has zero $H^j$. If $a>b$, the truncation is already zero. Taking $a=-n$ therefore proves $H^j(TK_n)=0$ for every $n\ge0$ and $j>b+c$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), last displayed triangle; Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological), with Definition 0147

proof.text:
For any fixed integer $r$, the same lower-truncation triangle with parameter $n+1$ gives
$$T(H^{-n-1}(K)[n+1])\longrightarrow TK_{n+1}\xrightarrow{T(u_n)}TK_n\longrightarrow T(H^{-n-1}(K)[n+2]).$$
Step 1 bounds the first term above by $c-n-1$. Thus, when $r>c-n-1$, its cohomology in degrees $r$ and $r+1$ is zero. Exactness of the segment from $H^r$ of the first term to $H^{r+1}$ of the first term makes $H^r(T(u_n))$ an isomorphism. Consequently, for every $r$ this cohomology tower has invertible transitions for all $n\ge\max(0,c-r)$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), successive lower truncations; Tag 05RS and Definition 0147

proof.text: Exact countable products give countable products in D(A) and preservation of those products by each cohomology functor in D(B). Apply T directly to the distinguished Roos triangle supplied by left completeness. Its middle morphism is T(1-s); applying H^r gives (T followed by H^r)(1-s). The composite T followed by H^r preserves the original product, so the images of its projections form a limiting fan. This permits the splitting construction and the vanishing argument to be performed on H^r(T(product K_n)) itself, without transporting the triangle to a chosen product of the images.

source.place: Tag 07KC (lemma-products); Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit); Tag 0H72 (remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations), with the assumed left completeness

proof.text: Fix j > b+c. In the mapped Roos triangle, H^j(T(product K_n)) is zero: its mapped projection fan is limiting for the product of the zero objects H^j(TK_n), by step 2. Its long exact sequence has the segment H^(j-1)(TP) --H^(j-1)(T(1-s))--> H^(j-1)(TP) --> H^j(TK) --> H^j(TP)=0. It suffices that the first map be an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological), Definition 0147; Tag 07KC (lemma-products); Tag 08TC, the cohomology sequence of its triangle

proof.text: Work more generally with a product-preserving additive functor F and a tower whose mapped transitions F(f_n) are invertible for n >= N. For any source Q and maps p_n:Q -> F(K_n), construct maps v_n with v_n - v_(n+1) >> F(f_n) = p_n. Induct on N. When N=0, start v_0=0 and recursively put v_(n+1)=(v_n-p_n) >> inverse(F(f_n)); the equation follows by cancellation. For N+1, apply the induction hypothesis to the shifted tower K_(n+1), put v_(n+1)=w_n and v_0=p_0+w_0 >> F(f_0). Taking Q=F(product K_n) and p_n the mapped projections, the universal property of the preserved product supplies a map s with projections v_n. The projection equations defining the tower transition endomorphism then give s >> F(1-s)=identity. Hence F(1-s) is split epi. Apply this with F=T followed by H^(j-1), using step 3 for eventual invertibility. All recursions construct actual morphisms; no arbitrary existence witness or elementwise argument is used.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), transition-endomorphism formula; elementary recursive splitting for an eventually invertible tower (agent argument)

proof.text: In the exact segment of step 5, the epimorphism of step 6 makes the morphism into $H^j(TK)$ zero. Exactness there says that the kernel of $H^j(TK)\to0$ is zero, so $H^j(TK)=0$. This holds for every integer $j>b+c$, which is the asserted upper bound. Only finite truncation intervals were used in step 2, while step 3 and the Roos triangle handle the unbounded negative tail.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), cohomology of the Roos triangle; conclusion of the agent truncation argument

proof_origin.place: Proof (2), lower-tail upper bound. Lean proof by finite truncation induction, eventual invertibility, and a recursive splitting in the preserved product fan; directly map the Roos triangle, avoiding a separate homotopy-limit mapping theorem. Stacks Tags 08J5, 07KC, 05RS, 08TC.
